title: What Is a Satellite?

cues.text: When you hear the word satellite, what comes to mind?
Perhaps a spacecraft, a television dish, or an image of Earth taken from space.
A satellite is an object that travels around another object in space.
The Moon is a natural satellite because it orbits Earth.
Human-made satellites are spacecraft placed into orbit to perform particular tasks.
Others help with navigation, weather monitoring, scientific research, or observing Earth’s surface.
Earth observation satellites carry instruments that measure energy coming from Earth or reflected by its surface.
Scientists use these measurements to study vegetation, water, cities, clouds, and many other features.
A satellite is more than a camera floating above Earth.
Its instruments collect specific kinds of information, and the data must be transmitted, processed, and interpreted before it becomes useful to us.
Satellites are valuable because they allow us to collect observations from space and use them to answer questions about our planet.
